proof: Governance replays the same acknowledgement for an identical handoff and rejects an idempotency-key payload mismatch.
Policy-learning recovers a failed acknowledgement without creating a duplicate candidate.
Unknown or unauthorized handoff queues fail closed before consumption.
Partial acknowledgement and stale successful ticks project degraded scheduler health.
Repository-published staging or production placeholder tokens are rejected under enforced posture.
Governance requires the exact handoff id, tenant, service actor, and idempotency binding.
Policy-learning accepts success only when the acknowledgement names the exact leased handoff ids.
Durable Governance and Agora stores preserve acknowledgement and lease state across client reconstruction.
Policy-learning replays an unacknowledged lease in a later intake window without duplicating its candidate.
Operators can pause the consumer while unacknowledged leases remain visible and health remains degraded.
Root compose activation remains outside this PR, so component rollback does not require a production or live-capital mutation.
